title: UniPercept: Towards Unified Perceptual-Level Image Understanding across Aesthetics, Quality, Structure, and Texture
claim: A benchmark is organized as a hierarchy of domains and criteria, each grounded in concrete image-question-answer examples.
layout: Central radial sunburst chart surrounded by a ring of example QA cards
description: A large circular sunburst chart sits at the center. Its three color-coded wedges are labeled IAA (red/pink), IQA (blue), and ISTA (purple), with a magnifying-glass-and-image icon in the middle. Outer rings divide each domain into categories and criteria, for example Composition & Design, Distortion Type, and Material Representation. Around the sunburst is a frame of tinted cards, each holding a photo, a question, and an answer. The card colors match the domain they belong to. The cards include rating questions (score 0–100) and multiple-choice or open-ended VQA questions. A header at the top shows GitHub and Hugging Face links for the code, benchmark, and checkpoint. The eye goes first to the bold central wheel and then to the colorful example cards around it.
caption: Overview of UniPercept-Bench. We propose a unified benchmark for perceptual-level image understanding, covering three perceptual domains: Image Aesthetics Assessment (IAA), Image Quality Assessment (IQA), and Image Structure and Texture Assessment (ISTA). Each domain is organized hierarchically into Domain–Category–Criterion levels, enabling fine-grained perceptual evaluation. The benchmark contains both Visual Rating (VR) and Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks, facilitating comprehensive assessment of models’ abilities to understand and reason about perceptual-level image understanding.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in visual understanding tasks such as visual grounding, segmentation, and captioning. However, their ability to perceive perceptual-level image features remains limited. In this work, we present UniPercept-Bench, a unified framework for perceptual-level image understanding across three key domains: Aesthetics, Quality, Structure and Texture. We establish a hierarchical definition system and construct large-scale datasets to evaluate perceptual-level image understanding. Based on this foundation, we develop a strong baseline UniPercept trained via Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training and Task-Aligned RL, enabling robust generalization across both Visual Rating (VR) and Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks. UniPercept outperforms existing MLLMs on perceptual-level image understanding and can serve as a plug-and-play reward model for text-to-image generation. This work defines Perceptual-Level Image Understanding in the era of MLLMs and, through the introduction of a comprehensive benchmark together with a strong baseline, provides a solid foundation for advancing perceptual-level multimodal image understanding.
